## Historical audit: S0292

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0005/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; observations are not split, so their supplied offsets cover whole lines.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1, `model_request` [0,11519) | Reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate SceneAct meshes and matching camera, framing, colors and materials. The student interpreted it as a classroom; that interpretation is not independent verification of the unseen reference. |
| Initial build — lines 3–4, H `model_response` and `execute` [0,9514), [0,9249) | The program constructs multiple objects: architecture, windows, five cabinets, tables, stools, trays, blocks and rug. Named child parts include cabinet panels and dividers and furniture legs. Colors and floor seams are specified, but no image texture is used. Placement is coded; actual contact, occlusion and pose fidelity are not geometrically verified. |
| First review and revision — lines 9, 11, 13–14 [0,23196), [0,44539), [0,9115), [0,8849) | Step 1 returned `ok: true` and a render was supplied to H. H described a distant cutaway, obstructing right wall and undersized furniture; these are student assessments, not independently viewed evidence. It changed camera and room dimensions, colors and lighting, added window and chair-back geometry, and executed the revision. |
| Second review and revision — lines 19, 21, 23–24 [0,27171), [0,81165), [0,8786), [0,8520) | Step 2 also rendered successfully and was supplied to H. H reported exposed room edges, a blank wall and washed-out surfaces. It expanded the floor and wall, adjusted camera and reduced lights, darkened colors, and replaced chairs with stools; this revised program was executed. It also requested 64 samples and 1920×1080, but the runner log reports 16 samples, so those requested settings cannot be assumed effective. |
| Outcome — lines 26, 28–30 [0,1607), [0,1596), [0,26920), [0,59) | Step 3 built and rendered with return codes zero and `ok: true`; step 3 was selected. This is **technical execution success**, not formal visual or geometric success. No final image review, correctness score, or `DONE` is recorded. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No separate teacher diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student message appears in this student trajectory; adoption of teacher advice is therefore unestablished. The system instructions and runner feedback were actually provided, but are not evidence of a separate teacher intervention. H independently produced three programs and two render-based revisions; sessions report no observable tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22 [0,3728), [0,4241), [0,4747)).

**Uncertainty and lessons.** The audit contains image paths, not viewable pixels: object completeness, texture realism, connectedness, chair orientation, camera match, lighting quality and whether the final changes improved the result remain unresolved. The student's cutaway and washout diagnoses are hypotheses grounded in its reported review, not independent findings. Transferably, successful rendering and named hierarchies establish neither scene fidelity nor correct part contact; preserving a complete scene while testing framing is observable here. The specific window counts, furniture layout and lighting adjustments are task-specific, not general prescriptions.
